title: Lifting it off the tram rail into the sun

tokens.v: Full-bleed photograph filling the entire frame edge to edge with no border, frame, letterbox band or matte of any kind. Exactly one phone in frame: one continuous tangerine polycarbonate unibody, no case, no second device, no notch or cutout, two stacked lenses and one flash in a single moulded tangerine pill. Its back is square to camera; the display face is turned away and not visible anywhere. A hand lifts it off the varnished timber rail of an old hillside tram as a bar of low sun crosses the rail, thumb and index finger pinching the lower-left corner, the rest of the hand curled out of frame below, the shell tipping out of the rail's shadow so the glossy tangerine ignites against dark wood. 50mm at f/2 at rail height from the seat opposite in the last hour before sunset, phone low right at a third of the frame, sun straight through the open window from camera-left, cane seat backs dissolving away. Only that hand and a forearm in a pushed-up ecru sleeve enter frame; the right edge cuts the sleeve, the rail runs out the bottom, the upper sash cuts the top. The shell is unmarked.
